attributes.title: Free Friday Nights Artmaking
attributes.description:
How might you combine materials into a collection that remembers or memorializes someone or something special to you? 

Stop by the ArtSpace for a free artmaking program honoring artist Agosto Machado, whose work is on view on Floor 6 as part of Whitney Biennial 2026. Participants are invited to assemble mixed materials to create commemorative items inspired by Machado's shrines and altars. Supplies will be provided, and no previous art experience is required—everyone is welcome.

Admission is free to all visitors every Friday evening from 5–10 pm. In addition to artmaking, join us for world-class exhibitions of contemporary American art, cocktails with views at Studio Bar, and more.

attributes.title: Whitney Signs: Minnie Evans
attributes.description:
Join us for an in-person tour of The Lost World: The Art of Minnie Evans led by Deaf educator Joyce Hom in American Sign Language. The event begins with a tour at 3:30 pm and will be followed by a wine and cheese reception from 5–6 pm in the Laurie M. Tisch Education Center. Please plan to meet in the Hearst Artspace on Floor 3 at 3:15 pm. 

This tour will be in ASL and will not have voice interpretation. To request interpretation for Tactile, Protactile, International Sign Language, another language, or additional accommodations, including Braille, please email accessfeedback@whitney.org or call (646) 666-5574 (relay calls welcome) with two weeks’ notice.

attributes.title: Educator Open House
attributes.description:
New York City educators are invited to learn about the Whitney’s education programs and explore how to use the museum as a resource for teaching.  

Throughout the evening, inquiry-based tours and guided close-looking experiences will be offered. Whitney educators will be available to speak about school and college and university visits, youth programs, and internships, as well as opportunities for cross-curricular learning and our bilingual offerings. Guests will also have the chance to hear from Chancellor of NYCPS, Kamar H. Samuels. The Open House will take place throughout the museum, with different activities on each floor. 

This event is open and free to K–12 teachers, high school teachers, university faculty, community educators, and anyone with a pedagogical practice who would like to utilize the Whitney for their teaching.

attributes.title: Walter Annenberg Lecture: Alex Da Corte
attributes.description:
Alex Da Corte is a Venezuelan-American artist inspired by Pop Art and Surrealism and informed by American cultural references. He is the co-curator of Roy Lichtenstein: Like New, which presents a retrospective of Lichtenstein in the contemporary context of accelerated production and circulation of images. For this Walter Annenberg Lecture, Alex Da Corte presents a talk about his engagement with Lichtenstein, combining his experiences as an artist and curator.

A conversation between the artist and Scott Rothkopf, Alice Pratt Brown Director, follows the presentation.   

Alex Da Corte (b. 1980) was born in Camden, New Jersey, and lives and works in Philadelphia. His work was included in the 2019 Venice Biennale and the 2018 Carnegie International in Pittsburgh, and he was selected as the 2021 Roof Garden Commission at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York. Past one-person exhibitions include the Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth, the Secession in Vienna, the 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art in Kanazawa, Japan, Fondazione Prada in Milan, and the Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in Humlebæk, Denmark.

attributes.title: Live Music by Marc Ribot
attributes.description:
6:30 pm
8 pm

Join the Whitney for a performance by Marc Ribot at Free Friday Nights, co-presented by Brooklyn-based performance venue and community space Public Records. 

Marc Ribot, who The New York Times describes as “a deceptively articulate artist who uses inarticulateness as an expressive device,” has released 25 albums under his own name over a 40-year career, exploring everything from the pioneering jazz of Albert Ayler to the Cuban son of Arsenio Rodríguez. In 2025, Ribot released “Map of a Blue City,” a collection of songs that features Ribot’s imaginative playing and leads to what may be his definitive statement as an instrumentalist, as a songwriter, and even as a singer. Jazzwise Magazine’s 4-star review states, “Ribot needs no introduction. But nothing prepares us for Map of a Blue City... Beyond jazz, steeped in humanity... an album of the year.”

Admission is free to all visitors every Friday evening from 5–10 pm. In addition to music, join us for world-class exhibitions of contemporary American art, cocktails with views at Studio Bar, and more.

attributes.title: Whitney Descriptions Online: Minnie Evans
attributes.open_to: Open to blind and low vision visitors
attributes.description:
Join us for a virtual program featuring The Lost World: the Art of Minnie Evans, led by educator Stina Puotinen. The tour begins at 11:30 am on Zoom.  

Whitney Descriptions Online provides an opportunity for visitors who are blind or have low vision to experience the richness and diversity of twentieth- and twenty-first-century American art through vivid description. Ninety-minute sessions are free of charge and are offered monthly on weekend mornings through Zoom and over the phone.

For all accommodations, please email accessfeedback@whitney.org or call (646) 666-5574 with two weeks’ notice.

attributes.title: Art + You
attributes.description:
Join us for a conversation about Aziz Hazara’s Moon Sightings (2024) in the Whitney Biennial 2026. Hazara’s work uses found materials and images drawn from night vision goggles that remained in Afghanistan in the aftermath of the American withdrawal. Together, we will use art as a window to explore the disruptions of war and surveillance alongside memory, place, and the limits of power and knowledge.

Art + You welcomes younger adults to share thoughts on artworks on view through close looking and dialogue. These gatherings are a unique way to experience art at the Whitney and make new connections. 

Upcoming Art + You programs will take place on:
November 6
December 4
January 8

Facilitator:
Caitlin Chan is a Ph.D. candidate in Art History at Stanford University. Her research on modern and contemporary American art is driven by questions of permanence, irrevocability, and wonder. At Stanford, Caitlin is a recipient of the Jeanette and William Hayden Jones Fellowship in American Art and Culture. She is also a Leadership in Inclusive Teaching fellow at Stanford's Center for Teaching and Learning. Previously, Caitlin has worked at the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden, Gallery 102, and Christie’s Auction House.

attributes.title: Halloween Member Night: Pop Party
attributes.description:
Celebrate Roy Lichtenstein: Like New and the artist’s 103rd birthday with a special costume party! Members are invited to experience our full exhibition lineup after hours with artmaking, live music, and more. Artful costumes encouraged—take inspiration from Roy and Dorothy Lichtenstein’s reimagining of Pop art celebrities Andy Warhol and Edie Sedgwick and join us as your favorite artist, artwork, or icon that inspires you.

Enjoy after-hours access to the galleries and mini tours throughout the evening.

attributes.title: Storytime
attributes.description:
The Whitney Free Second Sundays Storytime series continues strong, teaming up with independent bookstores to showcase diverse voices and fresh perspectives that will captivate our youngest visitors.

We're excited to launch a fantastic four-month partnership with Librería Comunitaria Barco de Papel and Centro Cultural, a vibrant community-run bookstore and cultural center. Their mission is to bring the magic of the Spanish language and bilingual literature to the heart of Flushing and Elmhurst, Queens—and now, right here at the Whitney!

Join us for Storytime with the incredible Paula Ortiz, co-founder of Barco de Papel, along with our passionate volunteer readers. They'll be bringing to life stunning art-inspired books that celebrate the beauty of storytelling in both Spanish and English. Don’t miss out on this unforgettable experience—be a part of a celebration that honors the future of storytelling with us!

En español

La serie Hora del Cuento, parte del Segundo domingo gratuito del Whitney, sigue creciendo, en colaboración con librerías independientes para destacar voces diversas y nuevas perspectivas que cautivarán a nuestros visitantes más jóvenes.

Nos entusiasma dar inicio a una fantástica colaboración de cuatro meses con Barco de Papel, una vibrante librería y centro cultural gestionada por la comunidad. Su misión es llevar la magia del idioma español y la literatura bilingüe al corazón de Flushing y Elmhurst, Queens, ¡y ahora también aquí, en el Whitney!

Acompáñanos en la Hora del Cuento con la increíble Paula Ortiz, cofundadora de Barco de Papel, junto con nuestros apasionados lectores voluntarios. Darán vida a maravillosos libros inspirados en arte, que celebran la belleza de la narración tanto en español como en inglés. No te pierdas esta inolvidable experiencia: ¡sé parte de una celebración que honra el futuro de la narración de cuentos!

attributes.title: Exhibition Tour: Whitney Biennial 2026
attributes.description:
Gallery tours through the Whitney’s current exhibitions are offered each day. Join a museum docent for insight into the works on view. See events calendar for timings. 

Tours are free with Museum admission. No reservations are necessary, but capacity is limited to twenty-five people on a first-come, first-served basis. Tours meet in the galleries. 

Times and locations are subject to change or cancellation. Please confirm daily tour times on our calendar.
